chunks: And informed us Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim, from Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Nuh, from Abu Nasr Hibatullah ibn Muhammad al-Katib, who said: Narrated to me Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Tarbak al-Rahawi, who said: Narrated to me Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh, or he said Abu al-Hasan (Ali ibn) Ahmad al-Dallal al-Qummi, who said:

A group of the Shia differed regarding whether Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, delegated to the Imams (peace be upon them) the ability to create or to provide sustenance? Some said: This is impossible! It is not permissible for Allah, the Exalted, because only Allah can create bodies. Others said: Rather, Allah, the Exalted, enabled the Imams to do this and delegated it to them, so they created and provided sustenance. They disputed this with intense dispute. One said: Why do you not refer to Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari and ask him about this, so that the truth becomes clear to you, for he is the way to the Master of the Command (Imam Mahdi), may Allah hasten his relief? The group agreed to Abu Ja'far, accepted his invitation, and responded to his statement. They wrote the question and sent it to him, and a decree (tawqi') came out to them from his side, the text of which was:
There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.

Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is He who created the bodies and distributed the sustenance, because He is not a body nor does He dwell in a body. And as for the Imams (peace be upon them), they ask Allah, the Exalted, and He creates; they ask Him and He provides sustenance, as a fulfillment of their request and to honor their right.

key_terms.إِجْبَارًا: As a fulfillment or due to
key_terms.تَوْقِيع: Decree or epistle from the Imam

ai.seo_question: Do the Imams create and provide sustenance independently or through Allah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* records a specific theological dispute among Shia scholars regarding whether the Imams possess independent creative power (*khalq*) and provision (*rizq*) or merely intercede. Imam al-Mahdi’s response clarifies the orthodox position: Allah is the sole Creator who is not a body, while the Imams’ act of asking is a divine honorific mechanism to elevate their status, distinguishing their role from independent agency.
